It is exactly the regression class fixed in iterations 062-100 (cf. iteration-096.md: 'diverges from the accessibility pattern used across Goals/Investments/Cashflow/Accounts/Settings/Analytics/Dashboard').

objectives.title: Announce client-side form-validation errors to assistive technology
objectives.evidence:
src/app/(auth)/register/page.tsx:79-80 and src/app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx:83 render validation failures inside a plain `

{error}

` with NO `role="alert"` and NO `aria-live`, so screen readers do not announce 'Passwords do not match' or bcrypt-boundary errors. This diverges from the established contract where settings/cashflow/accounts error regions correctly use `role="alert"` (e.g. settings/page.tsx:227, cashflow/page.tsx:273).
objectives.implementation_plan: Convert the register/reset-password (and login if added) error containers to `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"` (or reuse a shared `FormError` component). objectives.title: Guarantee one top-level h1 per page for screen-reader navigation
objectives.evidence: Grep for `<h1` across page.tsx shows budget, goals, analytics, cashflow, settings, all four auth pages, and the root app/page.tsx have ZERO `<h1>` elements, while dashboard/accounts/investments/smtp already expose a single h1 (via PageHeader or inline). Pages with no h1 break AT heading navigation and the document outline, and most of these pages also lack a visible page title element for non-sighted users.
objectives.implementation_plan: Standardize every app route on the existing `PageHeader`/`h1` contract: wrap budget/goals/analytics/cashflow/settings headers in PageHeader (eyebrow+title+description), and give the auth pages a single h1 (currently AuthShell renders only a title prop, not an h1). Add a lightweight lint/test asserting exactly one h1 per route module. Validate with tsc/lint/jest; no behavioral change.

objectives.title: Convey financial status without relying on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
objectives.evidence: src/app/budget/page.tsx communicates state through color only in several places: the progress bar fill uses `bg-red-500`/`bg-amber-500`/`bg-blue-500`/`bg-green-500` (line 235) with no text alternative; remaining/over-budget text switches `text-green-400` vs `text-red-400` (lines 159, 242); investments/page.tsx renders return tone via the color-only class `is-${previewPresentation.tone}` (line 432). Color-blind users cannot distinguish these states. Some labels exist ('Over Budget!', 'All good') but the bar ratio and remaining amounts are color-only.
objectives.implementation_plan: Add text/icon equivalents alongside color cues: an accessible label on the progress bar (e.g. `aria-label` '82% of budget used, over by Rp X' or a visible percentage + state word), and ensure remaining/over amounts include a textual state token, not just a color class. Verify the `is-${tone}` investment class also carries a text label. Add component tests for the textual alternatives. Validate via tsc/lint/jest; no financial-calculation change.
